rules.title: No unwrap on fallible runtime values
rules.body: Do not call unwrap() or expect() on Results and Options that can fail at runtime (I/O, parsing, user input, network); propagate with ? and add context. unwrap is fine in tests and for values proven present a line above (say why in a comment).

rules.title: Errors carry context
rules.body: Errors returned from library code are typed (thiserror) and application code adds context to them (anyhow::Context) saying what was being done.

rules.title: Every unsafe block has a SAFETY comment
rules.body: Each unsafe block is preceded by a // SAFETY: comment explaining why the invariants hold. Do not add unsafe code when a safe alternative exists.

rules.title: No blocking in async code
rules.body: Async functions do not call blocking APIs (std::fs, std::thread::sleep, blocking HTTP clients, heavy CPU loops); use the async equivalents or spawn_blocking. No lock guard is held across an .await.

rules.title: Checked arithmetic on input-driven values
rules.body: Arithmetic on values that come from input or external data uses checked_, saturating_ or wrapping_ operations as appropriate, and casts that can truncate use try_from.
